code.why: The life executes fetch in its in-memory World; listeners are exercised by standalone conformance.

RH2 is the demanded client-submitted ID-token sign-in and uses Apple. Only a World backed by the real Apple reaches this verified-token sign-in path: Apple's keys must verify the native token before the identity and session can be created. This World's GitHub and Google companions answer browser callbacks; it runs no twin of Apple, so its Apple keys fetch is refused and sign-in returns INVALID_TOKEN.

Every client a World registers is first-party with consent skipped, as Volter's products register at id.volter.ai (the app-credentials door and Open Autonomy's adminCreateClient both set skip_consent); a client that asks for consent is a World configured otherwise, and the consent screen is not served for it.

A returning GitHub sign-in whose profile names a new login updates the person's stored githubLogin (auth.ts mapProfileToUser). Only a live GitHub account renamed on github.com answers a new login: the github pack gives a person no rename, so a World's GitHub keeps each login it made.
